_comment: Functions that will never be matched by writing C, because they were not
produced by a C compiler. They are excluded from the work queue: without
this the scheduler keeps offering them, and they look like ideal targets
-- tiny, high fan-in, adjacent to easy matches. A wave-5 agent spent its
budget proving out this list, which is the only reason it exists.
Adding to this list is a claim that needs evidence in the reason field.
'I could not match it' is not evidence; the tells are in the
'not compiler output' section of docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
Cheap pre-filter when scoping a new batch:
grep -n 'arm_func_start\|non_word_aligned_thumb_func_start' asm/<file>.s
The strongest tell is the CALLING CONVENTION, but it is corroborating
evidence and not proof, and the paragraph near the end of this comment
explains why: a dead leading parameter is invisible in the body, so from
the assembly alone you CANNOT distinguish 'r0 was skipped' from 'r0 held
an argument nothing reads'. Both look identical. Any entry resting on the
parameter convention alone is therefore weaker than it reads.
Two things are still decisive on their own. A value RETURNED in a register
other than r0 is one -- dead arguments cannot explain a return register, so
sub_0807031C stands unaided. Two callable entry points inside one
instruction stream is the other.
What actually carries the nine ply_* handlers below is not that they take
the track pointer in r1. It is that register allocation DIFFERS across
structurally identical bodies within the block (sub_08071840 uses
r0-for-address / r2-for-byte and sub_08071868 the reverse), which one C
source shape cannot produce, plus their entry from a shared jump table.
Cite that, not the register, if you ever need to defend the block.
The m4a/MP2K driver spans roughly 0x0806F734-0x080718E4, with the linker
veneers immediately after. This comment used to say 'treat that whole span
as lift-from-another-decomp rather than re-derive'. That blanket claim is
WRONG and wave 8 disproved it: MPlayFadeOut (sub_080703D4) and
m4aMPlayFadeOutPause (sub_08070620) both matched as ordinary C. The span is
m4a.c (compiler output, matchable) interleaved with m4a_asm.s (hand-written,
never matchable) -- the same split every other GBA decomp has. Inside it:
a function the FE signature matcher has NAMED is almost certainly the m4a.c
side and is among the cheapest functions available, needing only that public
source be reconciled with this ROM's struct offsets; a function taking its
context in r1 is the m4a_asm.s side and belongs in this file.
Those two halves of the rule are not equally strong, and wave 9 found the
case where they collide: an FE NAME is not evidence of the m4a.c side, and
the calling convention still overrules it. sub_08070300 is FE-named
clear_modM and is hand-written; its compiled twin sits at sub_08071564 under
the FE name MP_clear_modM. The driver keeps BOTH copies of some routines, so
read the name as 'which routine is this', never as 'which half is it in'.
Check r0 first, every time.
Wave 10 measured how often that collides, on a batch of four FE-named
functions inside the span picked without regard to convention. THREE of the
four were hand-written -- sub_0806FC34 (ply_patt), sub_08070090
(ChnVolSetAsm) and sub_080717F8 (ply_xwave) -- and one, sub_08070AF8
(SoundVSyncOn_rev01), was ordinary C that matched first try. So an FE name
inside this span is not weak evidence of the m4a.c side, it is no evidence
at all; treat the name as free documentation of what the routine DOES and
settle the side from the registers. Two of the three announce themselves if
you read the name properly: ChnVolSetAsm says 'Asm' outright, and ply_* is
the jump-table handler family of which nine were already listed here.
Two tells beyond the calling convention showed up in that batch and are
worth adding to the list in docs/agbcc-codegen.md. A body that READS a
callee-saved register it never writes is taking an argument there:
sub_08070090 opens `ldrb r1,[r4,#0x12]` with no push at all, and
sub_080717F8 does `push {r4, lr}` and then `ands r4, r0` before ever
setting r4, so the pushed register is simultaneously an inbound operand.
And control flow that LEAVES the function -- sub_0806FC34 ends in two `b`s
to labels inside two other functions, and is itself the target of a `b` from
a jump-table stub. Neither is something a compiler emits, and both are
readable without knowing what the routine computes.
The calling-convention tell is about the FIRST parameter, and reading it as
'a context pointer in a register above r0' is too strong. sub_08020680 takes
its byte-stream pointer in r2 and never reads r0 or r1, which looks like the
ply_* shape and is not: it is void f(int, int, u8 *) with two dead leading
parameters, and it matched byte-for-byte. Dead arguments are ordinary C. The
tell only fires when the first LIVE parameter arrives somewhere r0 could have
held it -- i.e. when r0 is skipped with nothing occupying it.
The span's lower bound is real but tight. sub_0806F710, twenty bytes below
0x0806F734, is an ordinary Proc_StartBlocking wrapper: it takes its parent
in r0 like every other member of that family and matched byte-for-byte in
wave 9. Proximity to the driver is not evidence -- check the calling
convention before assuming a neighbour is resident.

functions.sub_0802C62A: Not code at all -- inter-function alignment padding. sub_0802C604 ends `bx r1` at 0x0802C628, and the two bytes at 0x0802C62A are the 0x0000 the assembler emits for `.align 2, 0` ahead of the 4-aligned sub_0802C62C. `movs r0, r0` is simply how 0x0000 disassembles. Zero callers.
functions.sub_0806F734: Hand-rolled mode switch (`add r2, pc, #0; bx r2`) at the head of the m4a/MP2K sound driver. Hand-written, not linker-generated.
functions.sub_0806F9A4: ARM code cut out as a THUMB unit. It sits between ARM instructions using r8/lr and `arm_func_start sub_0806F9AC`; the ARM stream above branches straight over it with `bgt sub_0806F9AC`. Its two halfwords are one ARM word. Note the usual grep does NOT catch this one -- it is a word-aligned `thumb_func_start`, not `non_word_aligned`; what gives it away is an `arm_func_start` immediately below and a body that reads registers it never sets and never returns.
functions.sub_0806F9A8: ARM code cut out as a THUMB unit, same as sub_0806F9A4 directly above it. Body is `movs r0, #4; lsls r0, r4, #0xe`, which reads r4 without setting it and has no `bx`. Reassembled as one ARM word, 0x03A02004 is `moveq r2, #4` -- what the m4a mixer actually executes.
functions.sub_0806FB66: m4a/MP2K sound driver. Not a function: a `bx r3` tail plus a literal pool, and the pool word is 0x68736D53 = "Smsh", the m4a ID_NUMBER that its apparent caller sub_0806F744 compares against. Same shape as sub_0807003C.
functions.sub_0806FBEC: m4a/MP2K sound driver, hand-written assembly. Three independent tells, none of which is a calling convention: (1) TWO callable entry points -- the body is `ldrb r3,[r2]` followed by the label _0806FBEE, and `bl _0806FBEE` appears four times in the file (once in sub_0806FCF8's predecessor and three times in a row at 0x0806FDxx) alongside `bl sub_0806FBEC`, so both halfwords are called; sub_0806FC0A also reaches _0806FBEE with a bare `b`. (2) It RETURNS IN r3 -- every caller does `bl _0806FBEE; str r3, [r1, #0xNN]` -- which no agbcc output does, the same tell already recorded for sub_0807031C. (3) It saves and restores r0 with an explicit `push {r0}` / `pop {r0}` INSIDE the body, which is not a frame agbcc builds. Body is the MP2K sample-pointer sanity check: it zeroes r3 unless r2 is below 0x02000000-ish (`lsrs r0,r2,#0x19`) or lies in the ROM window above gUnknown_081B9D64. Its r2 argument is NOT the evidence -- see the header note about sub_08020680.
functions.sub_0806FC08: m4a/MP2K sound driver, hand-written assembly. It is a single `ldr r2, [r1, #0x40]` that falls through into non_word_aligned_thumb_func_start sub_0806FC0A, and BOTH are bl targets -- two callable entry points two bytes apart in one instruction stream. See also sub_0806F740, a raw `.hword 0xFF1E` the disassembler could not decode.
functions.sub_0806FC34: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, hand-written assembly. FE-named ply_patt, and the name is not what settles it. Takes the MusicPlayerTrack pointer in **r1** with r0 never read, exactly like sub_0806FC50 (ply_pend) and the ply_* block at 0x08071840. Corroborated twice over by control flow that leaves the function: it ends in `b _0806FC14` and `b _0806FBA4`, both labels inside OTHER functions (_0806FC14 is a `push {lr}` entry point in the middle of sub_0806FC0A, _0806FBA4 is a `push {r4, r5, lr}` entry inside the routine before sub_0806FBEC), and it is itself branched INTO -- sub_0806F73C is `movs r0, r0; b _0806FC48`, a jump-table stub landing on this function's second-to-last instruction. A compiler emits neither. Field offsets it confirms: patternLevel at +0x02 (`ldrb r2,[r1,#2]`, bounded `cmp #3; bhs`), cmdPtr at +0x40, patternStack[] at +0x44 -- the same three sub_0806FC50 gives.
functions.sub_0806FC50: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, hand-written assembly. Takes the MusicPlayerTrack pointer in **r1**; r0 is never read, and agbcc passes the first parameter in r0 without exception. Same calling convention as the ply_* block at 0x08071840 and reached the same way. The body is ply_pend, and it names three MusicPlayerTrack fields at once: `ldrb r2,[r1,#2]` is patternLevel, `ldr r2,[r3,#0x44]` indexes patternStack[] after `lsls r2,#2`, and `str r2,[r1,#0x40]` is cmdPtr -- the same cmdPtr offset already recorded for sub_0806FC08 and the whole ply_* block. Its neighbour sub_0806FC64 (not split out separately) takes r1 the same way and falls into sub_0806FC16.
functions.sub_08070090: m4a/MP2K ChnVolSet, hand-written assembly -- the FE name ChnVolSetAsm says so and the body confirms it independently. It takes BOTH its operands in callee-saved registers it never writes: the first instruction is `ldrb r1, [r4, #0x12]` and it later reads `ldrb r0, [r5, #0x10]`, with r4 and r5 arriving live and r0-r3 all dead on entry. There is no `push`, so those are not saved values being restored -- they are inbound arguments. agbcc passes arguments in r0-r3 and treats r4-r7 as callee-saved, so no C source reaches this; it is a subroutine spliced into callers that have already set up the channel (r4) and track (r5) pointers, which is exactly what its two callers sub_0806FDE4 (MPlayMain) and sub_080700C0 (ply_note) do. Body is the stereo volume computation: `chan->rightVol = min(0xff, (env * (0x80 + pan) * track->volMR) >> 14)` and the mirrored `0x7f - pan` for the left, so it also pins three offsets -- +0x12 and +0x14 (SIGNED pan, `movs r0,#0x14; ldrsb r2,[r4,r0]`) on the channel, +0x10/+0x11 on the track, and the two results stored at channel +2/+3.
functions.sub_08070300: m4a/MP2K ClearModM, the hand-written copy. Takes the MusicPlayerTrack pointer in **r1**; r0 is never read. Both call sites confirm it directly: sub_080700C0 (ply_note) does `adds r1, r5, #0; bl sub_08070300` with r0 untouched, and sub_08070328 (ply_lfos) leaves r1 alone across `bl sub_0807031C` -- itself asm-resident -- and calls in with `mov ip, lr` standing in for the frame. The decisive corroboration is that the COMPILED copy of the same routine also exists, at sub_08071564: identical semantics, r0 convention, the two zero stores in the opposite order (0x1a then 0x16 rather than 0x16 then 0x1a), and the `orrs` destination on the constant rather than on the loaded flags. One C source cannot produce both, and only the r0 one is compiler output. This is the m4a.c / m4a_asm.s split, not a hard function.
functions.sub_0807003C: m4a/MP2K sound driver. Not a function at all: the `bx r3` tail of the routine above it plus a literal pool. The split drew a unit boundary mid-function.
functions.sub_0807031C: m4a/MP2K sound driver, hand-written assembly. Returns its result in r3 rather than r0, which no agbcc output does.
functions.sub_080717F8: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, hand-written assembly. FE-named ply_xwave, and it is the same ply_* family as the 0x08071840 block below rather than the m4a.c side the name might suggest. Two tells. It takes the MusicPlayerTrack pointer in **r1** (`ldr r2, [r1, #0x40]` first instruction, r0 never read) and it reads **r4 uninitialised**: after `push {r4, lr}` the very next use of r4 is `ands r4, r0`, so the incoming r4 is an operand, and the `pop {r4}` then throws the result away -- a register that is simultaneously an inbound argument and callee-saved is not something a compiler emits. Body assembles a 32-bit word out of four unaligned bytes at track->cmdPtr, one `ldrb`/shift/mask-and-or per byte with pool words 0xFFFFFF00 / 0xFFFF00FF / 0xFF00FFFF / 0x00FFFFFF, stores it to track +0x28 and advances cmdPtr by 4. The byte-at-a-time assembly with explicit clear masks is itself the m4a_asm.s idiom: agbcc would emit a single `ldr` for an aligned word and would not clear a field it is about to overwrite entirely.
functions.sub_08071840: m4a/MP2K track-command handler (`ply_*`), hand-written assembly. Takes the MusicPlayerTrack pointer in **r1**, not r0 -- agbcc passes the first parameter in r0 without exception, so no C source compiles to this. Body reads one byte from track->cmdPtr at [r1, #0x40], stores it to a track field, and advances cmdPtr. Same cmdPtr shape already recorded for sub_0806FC08. Entered from a jump table, which is why the whole block shares r1. Corroborating: register allocation differs across structurally identical bodies in this block (sub_08071840 uses r0-for-address / r2-for-byte, sub_08071868 the reverse), which one C source shape cannot produce. NOT evidence, do not cite it: the 12-byte members omit a cmdPtr reload the others perform -- that is only the `strb` displacement limit of 31, since offsets >=0x20 must materialise the address into a register and clobber r0. Field offset here: 0x24.
functions.sub_08071854: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, same block and same evidence as sub_08071840. Field offset 0x2c.
functions.sub_08071868: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, same block and same evidence as sub_08071840. Field offset 0x2d.
functions.sub_0807187C: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, same block and same evidence as sub_08071840. Field offset 0x2e.
functions.sub_08071890: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, same block and same evidence as sub_08071840. Field offset 0x2f.
functions.sub_080718A4: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, same block and same evidence as sub_08071840. Field offset 0x1e (fits the strb displacement, hence 12 bytes rather than 20).
functions.sub_080718B0: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, same block and same evidence as sub_08071840. Field offset 0x1f (fits the strb displacement, hence 12 bytes rather than 20).
functions.sub_080718BC: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, same block and same evidence as sub_08071840. Field offset 0x26.
functions.sub_080718D0: m4a/MP2K track-command handler, same block and same evidence as sub_08071840. Field offset 0x27.
functions.sub_080718E8: Linker THUMB->ARM interworking veneer: `bx pc; nop` plus an arm_func_start holding `b sub_08000304`. The 4-byte unit the index reports is only the THUMB half of an 8-byte veneer, cut at the mode change. The linker synthesises these when a THUMB bl targets an ARM symbol; no C construct emits one.
